text:
Consider the following example:
 Acalypha ostryifolia is a plant in the Euphorbiaceae family and is commonly known as hophornbeam copperleaf or pineland three-seed mercury. It is a native of North and Central America and is generally considered a weed.
Which is the topic of this example, Mean Of Transportation or Plant?
Plant.

Consider the following example:
 Sons of the Desert is a 1933 American film starring Laurel and Hardy and directed by William A. Seiter. It was first released in the United States on December 29 1933 and is regarded as one of Laurel and Hardy's greatest films.
Which is the topic of this example, Film or Natural Place?
Film.

Consider the following example:
 Doraksan is a mountain of Chungcheongbuk-do South Korea. It has an elevation of 964 metres
Which is the topic of this example, Natural Place or Album?
Natural Place.

Consider the following example:
 Opuntia matudae or xoconostle is a cactus native to Mexico.
Which is the topic of this example, Plant or Album?
Plant.

Consider the following example:
 Riddle High School is a public high school in Riddle Oregon United States.
Which is the topic of this example, Educational Institution or Athlete?
Educational Institution.

Consider the following example:
 John Edward Bruce also known as Bruce Grit or J. E. Bruce-Grit (February 22 1856 – August 7 1924) born a slave in Maryland United States became a journalist historian writer orator civil rights activist and Pan-African nationalist. He founded newspapers in Washington DC and Norfolk Virginia as well as co-founding the Negro Society for Historical Research in New York.
Which is the topic of this example, Artist or Village?
Village.

Consider the following example:
 Stratton is a lunar impact crater on the Moon's far side. It is located to the north of the large craters Keeler and Heaviside and less than one crater diameter to the south of Dewar.As with many craters on the Moon this feature has become worn and eroded due to a multitude of subsequent impacts of various sizes. The most prominent of these is a small cup-shaped impact along the southwestern outer rim.
Which is the topic of this example, Artist or Natural Place?
Artist.

Consider the following example:
 Eucalyptus gunnii (cider gum or gunnii) is a species of flowering plant in the family Myrtaceae endemic to Tasmania occurring on the plains and slopes of the central plateaux to around 1100 metres with isolated occurrences south of Hobart.It is a small- to medium-sized evergreen tree. Older specimens have a short massive bole and large spreading branches.
Which is the topic of this example, Plant or Written Work?
Plant.

Consider the following example:
 HMS Derwent was a Hunt class Type III destroyer escort of the Royal Navy. She was built by Vickers-Armstrongs Barrow-in-Furness and served during the Second World War.
Which is the topic of this example, Educational Institution or Mean Of Transportation?
Mean Of Transportation.

Consider the following example:
 Urge is a village in Kohila Parish Rapla County in northwestern Estonia.
Which is the topic of this example, Village or Animal?
Village.

Consider the following example:
 Cota Creek is a very minor tributary of the Upper Mississippi River. It is confined mainly to Taylor Township in Allamakee County Iowa United States. It joins the river at Harpers Ferry downstream from Lock and Dam No. 10.
Which is the topic of this example, Educational Institution or Natural Place?
Educational Institution.

Consider the following example:
 Tillandsia carnosa is a species of the genus Tillandsia. This species is native to Bolivia.
Which is the topic of this example, Album or Plant?
Album.

Consider the following example:
 The Warroad River is a tributary river of Lake of the Woods. It has its mouth in the City of Warroad Minnesota. The river is formed at the confluence of the East and West Branches Warroad Rivers south of the city of Warroad. Minnesota.
Which is the topic of this example, Natural Place or Mean Of Transportation?
Mean Of Transportation.

Consider the following example:
 Blaque By Popular Demand is a ten track compilation album of Blaque's most popular songs. Some of the group's hit singles (808 As If Bring It All to Me and Can't Get It Back) along with four selected tracks from their self-titled debut album and two remixes were featured on the compilation. Physical copies of the compilation were released to selected marketing stores such as Circuit City and were sold online via Amazon.
Which is the topic of this example, Album or Office Holder?
Album.

Consider the following example:
 Merlyn Alexis Membreño Flores (born June 24 1972 in Tegucigalpa) is a retired Honduran football defender.
Which is the topic of this example, Athlete or Company?
Athlete.

Consider the following example:
 Buddleja davidii var. alba is endemic to central and western China. The plant has also been treated as a form and a cultivar ('Alba'). However Anthonius Leeuwenberg sank var. alba and the other five varieties of davidii as synonyms considering them to be within the natural variation of a species a treatment also adopted in the Flora of China published in 1996.
Which is the topic of this example, Written Work or Plant?
Plant.

Consider the following example:
 The Cupido River is a river of Espírito Santo state in eastern Brazil.
Which is the topic of this example, Natural Place or Written Work?
Natural Place.

Consider the following example:
 Tom Tom Blues is the title of The 77s' eighth album released in 1995 on the Brainstorm Artists Intl label.
Which is the topic of this example, Album or Plant?
Plant.

Consider the following example:
 Mack Elwin Barham (June 18 1924 – November 27 2006) was a prominent attorney who served on the New Orleans-based Louisiana Supreme Court from 1968 to 1975.
Which is the topic of this example, Office Holder or Educational Institution?
Educational Institution.

Consider the following example:
 Alfonso Rumazo González (Latacunga 1903 – Caracas 2002) was an Ecuadorian writer historian essayist and literary critic.
Which is the topic of this example, Artist or Written Work?
Artist.

Consider the following example:
 Anderson House is the former residence of John Gary Anderson who was president of the Anderson Motor Company in Rock Hill South Carolina. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1982.
Which is the topic of this example, Building or Village?
Village.

Consider the following example:
 Chris Barth is an American Singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist originally from Indianapolis IN. He is best known for his work as principal songwriter and lead vocalist of the band The Impossible Shapes as well as his solo work under his own name and the alias Normanoak. He was also a member of the soul/punk band John Wilkes Booze.
Which is the topic of this example, Artist or Village?
Village.

Consider the following example:
 The Ogaal Newspaper (Somali: Wargeyska Ogaal) is an independent newspaper based in Hargeisa the capital of the northwestern Somaliland region of Somalia. Founded in 2005 it provides domestic news in both Somali and English. The outlet is part of the larger Ogaal Media Center that is headquartered in the city. Ogaal Newspaper is published daily except for Fridays.
Which is the topic of this example, Written Work or Village?
Written Work.

Consider the following example:
 The University of Klagenfurt (also Alpen-Adria-Universität Klagenfurt  AAU) is the largest education and research establishment in the Austrian province of Carinthia and has facilities in Klagenfurt Vienna and Graz. Efforts to develop the university began in 1964 and regular degree programmes commenced in 1973 during the tenure of provincial governor Hans Sima.
Which is the topic of this example, Natural Place or Educational Institution?
Natural Place.

Consider the following example:
 Brandbach is a river of North Rhine-Westphalia Germany.
Which is the topic of this example, Plant or Natural Place?
Plant.

Consider the following example:
 Invisible Cinema is an album by jazz pianist and composer Aaron Parks that was released on the Blue Note label on August 19 2008. The album is Parks' debut for Blue Note.
Which is the topic of this example, Village or Album?
Album.

Consider the following example:
 Mio Technology develops and markets GPS navigation mobile system services. The brand was established in May 2002 and now has operations in Taiwan mainland China Europe North America Australia Japan and South Korea. Mio currently employees 1200+ employees worldwide and sells and markets its products in over 56 countries and territories.
Which is the topic of this example, Educational Institution or Company?
Company.

Consider the following example:
 Gloria Trevi (born Gloria de los Ángeles Treviño Ruiz on February 15 1968) is a Mexican pop-rock singer-songwriter. Called the Supreme Diva of Mexican Pop by the music channel VH1 Trevi has sold more than 20 million records.
Which is the topic of this example, Natural Place or Artist?
Artist.

Consider the following example:
 Do U Know is the 3rd studio album of Hong Kong based singer Janice Vidal released on 21 November 2006. The title is named after Diana Ross's Theme from Mahogany (Do You Know Where You're Going To) which Vidal covers in the album. The album contains songs in both Cantonese and English. Music video in this album were extracts from the musical firm A Melody Looking.
Which is the topic of this example, Artist or Album?
Album.

Consider the following example:
 Mohsen Chavoshi Hosseini (Persian: محسن چاوشی‎) (born 30 July 1979) is an Iranian musician singer record producer and songwriter. He lives in Tehran.He has released 9 albums including a soundtrack to 2007 film Santouri.
Which is the topic of this example, Artist or Village?
Artist.

Consider the following example:
 Ernest Kwok Wong is an Australian politician and Australian Labor Party member of the New South Wales Legislative Council. Wong has been a member of the Council since 24 May 2013.
Which is the topic of this example, Film or Office Holder?
Film.

Consider the following example:
 John Griffiths AM (born 19 December 1956) is a Welsh Labour Co-operative politician and the Minister for Environment and Sustainable Development. Born in Newport Monmouthshire Griffiths has represented the constituency of Newport East since the National Assembly for Wales was established in 1999.
Which is the topic of this example, Office Holder or Animal?
Animal.

Consider the following example:
 Tolna sypnoides is a species of moth of the Noctuidae family.It is found in Africa including Nigeria Sierra Leone Ghana South Africa Madagascar and other islands of the Indian OceanThe caterpillars feed on Mango trees (Mangifera indica) Schinus terebinthifolius both of the family of Anacardiaceae and Syzygium cumini (Myrtaceae).Their wingspan is around 70mm.
Which is the topic of this example, Animal or Mean Of Transportation?
Mean Of Transportation.

Consider the following example:
 Daniel Cooley Uggla (born March 11 1980) is an American professional baseball second baseman with the Atlanta Braves of Major League Baseball. He previously played for the Florida Marlins.Uggla finished third in the 2006 National League Rookie of the Year voting behind teammate and winner Hanley Ramírez and Ryan Zimmerman of the Washington Nationals but won the Players Choice and Sporting News NL ROY awards.
Which is the topic of this example, Office Holder or Athlete?
Athlete.

Consider the following example:
 George Fredrick Wrighster III (born April 1 1981) is an American football tight end. He was drafted by the Jacksonville Jaguars in the fourth round of the 2003 NFL Draft. He played college football at Oregon.Wrighster has also been a member of the New York Giants.
Which is the topic of this example, Athlete or Animal?
Animal.

Consider the following example:
 For the mall in Dasmarinas under the same name see The District-DasmariñasThe District - Imus also known as District Mall - Anabu and previously known as 'The District - Cavite' is a shopping mall owned by the Ayala Land. It is the first Ayala Mall in the province of Cavite.
Which is the topic of this example, Building or Athlete?
Building.

Consider the following example:
 Technometrics is a journal of statistics for the physical chemical and engineering sciences published quarterly since 1959 by the American Society for Quality and the American Statistical Association.
Which is the topic of this example, Film or Written Work?
Written Work.

Consider the following example:
 Punisher MAX is the second comic book ongoing series published under the MAX imprint of Marvel Comics featuring the vigilante anti-hero the Punisher.
Which is the topic of this example, Animal or Written Work?
Written Work.

Consider the following example:
 Albizia edwallii is a species of legume in the Fabaceae family.It is found in Argentina and Brazil.
Which is the topic of this example, Plant or Film?
Plant.

Consider the following example:
 Josh Kennet (born 27 September 1987) is an English footballer.
Which is the topic of this example, Athlete or Album?
Athlete.

Consider the following example:
 Zia-ul-Haq (Urdu: ضیاء الحق‎; born 11 December 1994) is a young fast bowler. He is a Left Arm Fast Medium bowler who could bowl with significant pace. Recently he has been selected for Pakistan Under-19 cricket team.
Which is the topic of this example, Athlete or Building?
Athlete.

Consider the following example:
 Functions of Language is a peer-reviewed academic journal that covers the field of linguistics treated from a functional perspective. It has been published by John Benjamins since 1994. The current editors in chief are Martin Hilpert (University of Neuchâtel) J. Lachlan Mackenzie (Free University Amsterdam) and Geoff Thompson (University of Liverpool).
Which is the topic of this example, Written Work or Natural Place?
Written Work.

Consider the following example:
 Ahmad Balshe (Arabic: أحمد بلشي‎) (born April 7 1984) better known by his stage name Belly is a Palestinian Canadian Juno Award-winning rapper.Born in Jenin Palestine his musical career has been based in Ottawa Ontario. In addition to a Juno he has won three MuchMusic Video Awards and has twice attained a top chart position in the national Much Music Countdown. Belly has written many #1 and platinum gold/hits for other artists.
Which is the topic of this example, Artist or Educational Institution?
Artist.

Consider the following example:
 Charles J. Spencer Jr. (born March 17 1982 in Poughkeepsie New York) is an American football offensive tackle who is currently a free agent. He was drafted by the Houston Texans in the third round of the 2006 NFL Draft. He played college football at Pittsburgh.Spencer has also been a member of the Carolina Panthers Jacksonville Jaguars and Florida Tuskers.
Which is the topic of this example, Building or Athlete?
Athlete.

Consider the following example:
 Robert Richard Hieronimus Ph.D. (b. 1943) is an educator artist author activist and has been an acknowledged pioneer in the New Paradigm movement since 1971.
Which is the topic of this example, Mean Of Transportation or Artist?
Artist.

Consider the following example:
 Michael Merrifield is an American politician from the U.S. state of Colorado. He served four terms (2004-2010) as a Representative in House District 18. He was chairman of the House Education Committee and also served on the House Transportation and Energy Committee. After leaving the legislature in 2010 due to term limits he campaigned to serve as an El Paso County Commissioner in District 5 but lost.
Which is the topic of this example, Village or Office Holder?
Village.

Consider the following example:
 Shane Luitjens is a graphic designer photographer and writer based in New York City.
Which is the topic of this example, Album or Artist?
Artist.

Consider the following example:
 Rębiszewo-Zegadły [rɛmbiˈʂɛvɔ zɛˈɡadwɨ] is a village in the administrative district of Gmina Kołaki Kościelne within Zambrów County Podlaskie Voivodeship in north-eastern Poland.
Which is the topic of this example, Village or Company?
Village.

Consider the following example:
 Island Masters is a midprice CD series that includes re-releases of records from the 1970s and 1980s by PolyGram. In 1989 Island Records was sold to PolyGram. The series was released in the UK and Europe. In the UK the discs were released with the prefix IMCD and catalogue numbers starting with 1. In some European countries the catalogue numbers were the same and in some they were not. This series was not released in the US.
Which is the topic of this example, Office Holder or Company?
Office Holder.

Consider the following example:
 HMS Duncan was a D-class destroyer leader built for the Royal Navy in the early 1930s. The ship was initially assigned to the Mediterranean Fleet before she was transferred to the China Station in early 1935 where she remained until mid-1939. Duncan returned to the Mediterranean Fleet just after World War II began in September 1939.
Which is the topic of this example, Album or Mean Of Transportation?
Mean Of Transportation.

Consider the following example:
 The Western Painted Lady (Vanessa carye) is a butterfly of the Nymphalidae family. It is found in South America from the mountains of Colombia and west of Caracas (Venezuela) through Ecuador Peru Bolivia and Chile southern Brazil and Paraguay to Patagonia in Argentina. It is also found on Easter Island and Tuamotus.The larvae feed on Achyrocline flaccida.
Which is the topic of this example, Animal or Written Work?
Written Work.

Consider the following example:
 Canterbury University Online is a private degree-granting institution. According to its website Canterbury University was established in 1974 in Hyde-Cheshire Manchester United Kingdom. Is an independent university that delivers various specialized scientific courses.A diploma from Canterbury University Online is available by online class work transferred credits from another accredited university as well as documented work experience.
Which is the topic of this example, Educational Institution or Plant?
Plant.

Consider the following example:
 The second USS Wandank (ATA-204) originally USS ATA-204 was a United States Navy auxiliary ocean tug in commission from 1945 to 1947 and again from 1952 to 1971.
Which is the topic of this example, Mean Of Transportation or Artist?
Mean Of Transportation.

Consider the following example:
 Akuku is a mountain peak in Cordillera Apolobamba.
Which is the topic of this example, Natural Place or Plant?
Natural Place.

Consider the following example:
 For the Selwyn Range in the Canadian Rockies see: Selwyn Range (Canada). Note also the Selwyn Mountains on the border between the Yukon and Northwest Territories in Canada.The Selwyn Range (also known as the Isa Highlands) is a rugged mountain range near Mount Isa and Cloncurry in north-west Queensland Australia composed largely of Proterozoic metamorphic rocks.
Which is the topic of this example, Animal or Natural Place?
Natural Place.

Consider the following example:
 Tripodion is a genus of flowering plants in the legume family Fabaceae. It belongs to the subfamily Faboideae.
Which is the topic of this example, Plant or Educational Institution?
Educational Institution.

Consider the following example:
 The Schweizer SGS 1-23 is a United States Open and Standard Class single-seat mid-wing glider built by Schweizer Aircraft of Elmira New York.The original standard 1-23 was introduced in 1948. The aircraft quickly became the most numerous competition and performance sailplane in the USA. A total of 93 of all sub-models were built by the time production was completed in 1967.
Which is the topic of this example, Mean Of Transportation or Village?
Mean Of Transportation.

Consider the following example:
 László Domokos (born February 26 1965) is a Hungarian politician member of the National Assembly (MP) for Szarvas (Békés County Constituency V) from 1998 to 2010.He became President of the State Audit Office as a result he resigned from his parliamentary seat on July 4 2010. He was replaced by Béla Dankó after a by-election.
Which is the topic of this example, Plant or Office Holder?
Plant.

Consider the following example:
 Gerardus Mattheus Johannes (Gerard) Veldkamp (27 June 1921 in Breda – 15 September 1990 in Paris) was a Dutch politician and Professor of Study of Social Security at the Leiden University.
Which is the topic of this example, Building or Office Holder?
Office Holder.

Consider the following example:
 Woodsmen of the West is a novel by Martin Allerdale Grainger first published in 1908 by Edward Arnold. In writing the novel Grainger drew on his experiences as a logger working in the coastal forests of British Columbia Canada. Woodsmen of the West is one of the first examples of realism in western Canadian literature. Grainger based his novel on his unsentimental account of life in the logging camps.
Which is the topic of this example, Written Work or Film?
Film.

Consider the following example:
 Ravenscroft School is an independent formerly Episcopal college preparatory school located in Raleigh North Carolina. It enrolls students from pre-school through grade 12. Founded in 1862 by members of Christ Episcopal Church the school continued under their principles until 1969 when it became non-sectarian.
Which is the topic of this example, Educational Institution or Album?
Album.

Consider the following example:
 Domaine Dujac is a Burgundy wine producer. The domaine is run by the Seysses family; the founder Jacques Seyesses is still involved in its operation but his sons Jeremy and Alec and Jeremy's wife Diana have run the domaine for the past several vintages. Jacques founded the domaine in 1967 although the first release was 1969.
Which is the topic of this example, Athlete or Company?
Company.

Consider the following example:
 The American Educational Research Journal is a peer-reviewed academic journal that covers the field of educational research. The editor-in-chief is Teresa L. McCarty(University of California Los Angeles). It was established in 1964 and is currently published by American Educational Research Association in partnership with Sage Publications.
Which is the topic of this example, Written Work or Building?
Building.

Consider the following example:
 Samsung Research India - Bangalore (SRI - Bangalore) earlier known as Samsung Electronics India Software Operations (SISO) is one of the twelve Research & Development centers of Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. housed in the IT hub of India Bangalore. With its inception dating back to February 1996 as a liaison office today it has grown in magnitude and proportions as a location for research and software development encompassing a wide range of technology domains.
Which is the topic of this example, Written Work or Company?
Written Work.

Consider the following example:
 National College of Natural Medicine (NCNM) is a school of naturopathic medicine and Classical Chinese medicine located in Portland Oregon United States. Founded in 1956 it is the oldest programmatically of the seven accredited naturopathic medical schools in North America. Until July 1 2006 NCNM was known as the National College of Naturopathic Medicine.
Which is the topic of this example, Educational Institution or Written Work?
Educational Institution.

Consider the following example:
 Cross My Heart is the twenty-first novel in the Alex Cross series all written by author James Patterson. The novel itself actually takes place after Alex Cross Run in which Alex tries contemplating a life outside of Metro Police after the apparent death of Ava an orphan girl they took in. It was initially not planned by Patterson but was later confirmed to be in the works. The novel will once again feature Metro Police detective Alex Cross.
Which is the topic of this example, Village or Written Work?
Written Work.

Consider the following example:
 Gulf University for Science & Technology (GUST) is the first private university established in Kuwait. It has a dual-enrollment agreement with the University of Missouri–St. Louis.
Which is the topic of this example, Educational Institution or Athlete?
Athlete.

Consider the following example:
 The Whisky Creek Cabin is a rustic log cabin located in southwest Oregon along the section of the Rogue River that is designated as a National Wild and Scenic River. It is the oldest remaining mining cabin in the Rogue River canyon. The Bureau of Land Management purchased the cabin and surrounding property in 1973. The Whisky Creek Cabin is listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1975.
Which is the topic of this example, Building or Written Work?
Building.

Consider the following example:
 Podocoma is a genus of flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae.
Which is the topic of this example, Village or Plant?
Plant.

Consider the following example:
 Panther Lake Camping Resort is a camping resort in Northern New Jersey. The resort has a 45-acre lake on 160 acres. Panther Lake Campground is 50 miles away from New York City. Panther Lake offer four options cabins trailers people who tent and RV's. Panther Lake Camping Resort has a beach right on the lake and also has a pool and a hot tub. Guests are allowed to boat fish swim and hike kayak and canoe.
Which is the topic of this example, Office Holder or Company?
Company.

Consider the following example:
 James Edwin Ellerbe (January 12 1867 - October 24 1917) was a U.S.
Which is the topic of this example, Office Holder or Film?
Office Holder.

Consider the following example:
 Arnold Schwarzenegger's Total Body Workout is a 1983 musical compilation. The album has significant camp value amongst music collectors today due to Schwarzenegger's well recognised thick Austrian accent issuing fitness instructions layered on top of several 1980s feelgood hits such as Journey's Don't Stop Believin' and The Weather Girls It's Raining Men.
Which is the topic of this example, Album or Natural Place?
Natural Place.

Consider the following example:
 Hajjiabad (Persian: حاجي اباد‎ also Romanized as Ḩājjīābād and Ḩājīābād) is a village in Sanjabad-e Sharqi Rural District in the Central District of Khalkhal County Ardabil Province Iran. At the 2006 census its population was 139 in 37 families.
Which is the topic of this example, Office Holder or Village?
Office Holder.

Consider the following example:
 Lac Île-à-la-Crosse is a lake in northwest Saskatchewan on the Churchill River. It is basically Y-shaped. At the center of the Y is the town of Île-à-la-Crosse the second oldest town in Saskatchewan. The Churchill exits the northeast arm and flows east to Hudson Bay through a series of lakes. The Churchill enters at the northwest arm called Aubichon Arm or Deep River.
Which is the topic of this example, Company or Natural Place?
Company.

Consider the following example:
 Where Sleeping Dogs Lie is a 1991 thriller film directed by Charles Finch and starred Dylan McDermott Sharon Stone and Tom Sizemore. The primary location for Sleeping Dogs was C.E. Toberman Estate a large Mediterranean-style 22-room house built at the top of Camino Palmero in 1928 by C. E. Toberman.
Which is the topic of this example, Film or Office Holder?
Film.

Consider the following example:
 Eugen Elishiringa Mwaiposa (born 23 November 1960) is a Tanzanian CCM politician and Member of Parliament for Ukonga constituency since 2010. Born in Kilimanjaro Region Tanzania. Previous position held are Member of UWT Member of National executive committee and the secretary of finance all under CCM party. She is married to Ally Mwaiposa the couple have two daughters.
Which is the topic of this example, Company or Office Holder?
Company.

Consider the following example:
 Dar Gerdu (Persian: درگردو‎ also Romanized as Dar Gerdū) is a village in Howmeh Rural District in the Central District of Bam County Kerman Province Iran. At the 2006 census its population was 13 in 5 families.
Which is the topic of this example, Plant or Village?
Plant.

 Penguin Island (also known as Georges Island Île Pingouin Isla Pingüino and Penguin Isle) is one of the smaller of the South Shetland Islands of Antarctica.
Which is the topic of this example, Natural Place or Plant?
Plant.

Consider the following example:
 Osiny [ɔˈɕinɨ] is a village in the administrative district of Gmina Kępno within Kępno County Greater Poland Voivodeship in west-central Poland.
Which is the topic of this example, Company or Village?
Village.

Consider the following example:
 Luck in Pawn is a 1919 silent film romance starring Marguerite Clark and directed by Walter Edwards. It was produced by Famous Players-Lasky and distributed through Paramount Pictures. The film is based on a play by Marvin Taylor Luck in Pawn and ran briefly on Broadway in 1919. The film is listed as being preserved at the Library of Congress and New Zealand Film Archive.
Which is the topic of this example, Artist or Film?
Film.

Consider the following example:
 Cloak and Dagger is an album by Scratch The Upsetter released in 1973.
Which is the topic of this example, Album or Natural Place?
Natural Place.

Consider the following example:
 Small Beer Press is a publisher of fantasy and literary fiction based in Northampton Massachusetts. It also publishes the zine Lady Churchill's Rosebud Wristlet chapbooks the Peapod Classics line of classic reprints and limited edition printings of certain titles.
Which is the topic of this example, Company or Written Work?
Company.

Consider the following example:
 Peppino le modelle e chella là is a 1957 Italian comedy film directed by Mario Mattoli and starring Gino Bramieri.
Which is the topic of this example, Film or Educational Institution?
Film.

Consider the following example:
 Zorro The Gay Blade is a 1981 feature film. This comedy features George Hamilton in a Golden Globe-nominated dual role as both Don Diego de la Vega (Zorro) and his gay twin brother Bunny Wigglesworth né Ramon De La Vega.
Which is the topic of this example, Written Work or Film?
Written Work.

Consider the following example:
 Ticinepomis is an extinct genus of coelacanth lobe-finned fish which lived during the Triassic period. It belonged to the family of Coelacanthidae.
Which is the topic of this example, Animal or Building?
Building.

Consider the following example:
 Holiday is a Booker Prize-winning novel by English writer Stanley Middleton.

Written Work.

 Bituing Marikit is the first full-length film produced by Sampaguita Pictures released in 1938. Its stars were the Singing Sweetheart of the Philippines Elsa Oria and King of the Philippine Movies Rogelio de la Rosa.
Which is the topic of this example, Artist or Film?
Film.

Consider the following example:
 Yves Saint Laurent YSL (also known as Saint Laurent Paris) is a luxury fashion house founded by Yves Saint Laurent and his partner Pierre Bergé. The founder of the brand died in 2008 and had last produced the haute couture line in 2002.Founded in 1961 it has been considered one of the world's most prominent fashion houses and known for its modern and iconic pieces such as its tuxedo jackets for women.
Which is the topic of this example, Company or Album?
Company.

Consider the following example:
 Westmount Charter School is a charter school based in Calgary Alberta Canada; which educates gifted students from kindergarten to grade 12. It was founded in 1996 as ABC (Action for Bright Children) Charter Public School a school for gifted children. The school started with 116 students from grades one to three and is now hosting a gifted student body of over 1000 in grades Kindergarten through 12.
Which is the topic of this example, Animal or Educational Institution?
Animal.

Consider the following example:
 Det Nødvendige Seminarium (DNS) (English: The Necessary Teacher Training College) is a private teacher training college in Denmark. DNS is integrated part of the School Center Tvind and since 2011 DNS is in cooperation with One World University (OWU) in Mozambique which opened oportunity of new three year program with a degree of licentiate of pedagogy.The college is private and the students are self-financed within the framework of the college.
Which is the topic of this example, Artist or Educational Institution?
Artist.

Consider the following example:
 Mohammed Tukur Liman was elected Senator for the Katsina South constituency of Katsina State Nigeria at the start of the Nigerian Fourth Republic running on the People's Democratic Party (PDP) platform. He took office on 29 May 1999.After taking his seat in the Senate in June 1999 Liman was appointed to committees on Banking & Currency Communication (vice chairman) Education and Special Projects.He was appointed Senate Majority Leader.

Office Holder.

 In addition to published work this article also includes Denis Gifford's radio and television credits.
